title: Law and permits
purpose: Nobody films who should not film. No filing is late. When there is a breach, we tell the client and the regulator inside the time limit. If we fail at any one of these, the contract can end.
how: Compliance is a check we do at the site. It is not a folder of papers. Onboarding screening has seven lines. No device goes on anyone's head until every line is done. The site nominates the worker. KMSC decides if the worker is activated. The seven lines are on the onboarding screening page. This page explains what is behind them. Mano owns the gate. Mazen and the site's Portfolio Manager run the gate on launch day. Moharam does not certify a launch until Mano confirms that every wearer's file is complete.

The wearer file is our proof. There is one folder for each person. It holds the copy of their ID, the consent they signed, the signed fraud briefing, the account in their name, and every row of the wearer log that they appear in. The wearer log is what links a flag to a person and not only to a phone. The wearer log is also how we prove that the person whose face is in the footage gave consent. Mano keeps the file for as long as we hold footage of that person.

breaks.what: A worker at the site looks under 18 or has no ID
breaks.do: Do not give them a device. It does not matter who assigned them. Tell the Portfolio Manager. The Portfolio Manager tells Mano the same day. If the worker already filmed, take the device away that shift. Youssef Medhat holds every session from that device. Adham decides what we tell the client.

breaks.what: A wearer asks us to stop, or asks what data we hold about them
breaks.do: Filming of that person stops in the same shift. Mano answers with counsel. The Portfolio Manager does not promise anything at that moment.

breaks.what: A phone is lost with footage on it
breaks.do: Put the phone in lost mode within one hour, as the asset control page says. From that hour, we treat it as a suspected breach. Tell Mano and Moharam. Adham's 24-hour time limit to tell the client starts. If the phone is not found within 24 hours, wipe it. If we cannot prove the phone was locked, it is a breach, and we send the breach notice.

Mano tells Adham on the day the filing misses its date, not a week later. Counsel files it late and tells us what the late filing costs. Put the true new date on the calendar. A missed filing is something we report. It is never a secret.

breaks.what: It is October and a data-protection row is not filed
breaks.do: Adham, Mano, and counsel meet on October 1. They decide two things. First, they file what is ready. Second, they agree on how we will film and transfer footage on November 1 if the rest is not filed by then. The date does not move, so the plan must change.

questions.q: Is a video of someone working really personal data?
questions.a: Yes. A video shows a person's face, and that makes it personal data. This is why we need the consent, the signage, the licence, and the breach time limits.

questions.q: The site manager says the worker is fine, he just forgot his ID.
questions.a: Then he films tomorrow, when he brings his ID. The site nominates workers. KMSC decides who is activated. If there is no ID, there is no device. It does not matter who asks.

questions.q: Who calls the regulator, and who calls the client?
questions.a: Mano calls the regulator, with counsel. Adham calls the client. Nobody else calls the regulator or the client, for any reason.

questions.q: Why is the time limit for the client shorter than the time limit for the regulator?
questions.a: Because the contract says 24 hours. Without the contract there is no company. We work to the shorter time limit. If we meet the 24-hour limit, we meet the 72-hour limit too.

breach.owner: Mano with counsel to the regulator. Adham to the client.
breach.text: A breach is when footage or personal data is out of our control. A lost phone that we cannot prove was locked is also a breach. Whoever suspects a breach tells their Portfolio Manager right away. Moharam and Mano are told within one hour. Adham calls the client within 24 hours. Mano, with counsel, tells the regulator within 72 hours.

gateNote: Onboarding screening is the compliance check at the site. It has seven lines. No device goes on anyone until every line is done. The seven lines are on the onboarding page. This page explains what is behind them.
